findings: pyproject.toml declares license = {text = "Proprietary"} while the LICENSE file shipped in the same sdist is Apache License 2.0 and NOTICE exists; the metadata is also deprecated by setuptools (deadline 2027-02-18). NOT changed here: D18 requires an explicit reviewed licensing decision, which is a human action outside this work item.
Python floor is inconsistent: BUILDING.md says Python 3.10+ while pyproject.toml declares requires-python = ">=3.9"; only 3.14.7 was exercised.
The wheel carries the local tag linux_x86_64, not manylinux, so it is a host wheel; no portable wheel is produced.
Package version 0.5.2 is identical across builds, so install/upgrade/rollback cannot be expressed as a version change; SHA-256 of the wheel and of the installed _core*.so are the only build identity.

cmake/Install.cmake installs only the static core archive (ARCHIVE destination); no shared-library or runtime destination is declared, which is correct for the current static-only core but must change if BUILD_SHARED_LIBS is ever offered.
scripts/verify-release.sh writes only to evidence/local-verification-report.txt and evidence/environment-local.json, so any redirected execution must be declared (done above).
limitations: Single Linux x86-64 host, gcc 16.2.1 Release, Python 3.14.7, CPU only; clang attempted only through verify-release (see release_verification).
No hosted CI, no second machine, no CUDA device, no Windows/macOS/aarch64, no other Python version, no other distribution or glibc.
No SBOM, no signing, no vulnerability scan, no reproducible-build comparison, no dependency lockfile: all are IR-33 open items.
No support owner, no named maintainers, no security contact, no SLA: D18 is unfulfilled and IR-33 stays open.
The external consumer solves one small MILP from examples/cases and replays its proof; that is a smoke test, not a correctness campaign.
Test data for the consumer comes from the repository (examples/cases/multiperiod_production.mps); only the consumer project and the link/compile/run are external.
The sdist was built in a /tmp copy, not in the repository, to avoid rewriting the tracked python/markov_cero.egg-info/SOURCES.txt.
pytest/numpy are test-only tools installed from a local wheel directory; the markov-cero wheel install itself used --no-index --no-deps.
Rollback was proven at the wheel/binary level between two builds of the same version 0.5.2, not across a version downgrade.
